pageTitle: Using service-linked roles for AWS Artifact
whatThePageStates: The page explains the AWS Artifact service-linked role AWSServiceRoleForArtifact: what it is, which service principal trusts it, which AWS Organizations actions its managed policy allows, and how to create, edit and delete it. Almost all of the page is prose and procedure with no coverage content. The one coverage statement sits in the final section, 'Supported Regions for AWS Artifact service-linked roles', which opens with the explicit exclusion sentence 'AWS Artifact does not support using service-linked roles in every Region where the service is available' and then gives a three-column table (Region name, Region identity, Support in AWS Artifact) of 25 Regions, each marked Yes or No. Only 3 Regions are Yes; the other 22 are an explicit, stated No. There is no Partial value and no second dimension.

features.featureName: Supported Regions for AWS Artifact service-linked roles (AWSServiceRoleForArtifact)
features.statuses: 3 Yes, 22 No; 3+22=25. Yes = us-east-1, us-west-2, us-gov-west-1 (the role can be used there). No = the remaining 22 rows, and this is a STATED not-supported: the column literally reads 'No' and the section's lead sentence says AWS Artifact does not support service-linked roles in every Region where the service is available. No Partial, no blank, no footnote-qualified cell anywhere in the table.
features.scope: None. The table has exactly one status column and it applies to the single role AWSServiceRoleForArtifact. There is no per-plan, per-partition or per-account-type split, though the row set does mix commercial Regions with two GovCloud Regions (us-gov-east-1 No, us-gov-west-1 Yes) inside the same list.
features.reasoning: Every row names one AWS Region by name and Region identifier, and the enumerated universe (AWS Regions) exists independently of AWS Artifact, so the axis is region and the kind is external. The unit of claim is one Region per row: 25 rows, 25 distinct Region identifiers, no duplicates and no service or resource sub-rows, so the rows do not collapse and distinctTargets/collapse are omitted.

shouldNotExtract: The four AWS Organizations API actions the role policy allows (DescribeOrganization, DescribeAccount, ListAccounts, ListAWSServiceAccessForOrganization) are the contents of a permissions policy, not a coverage claim about what AWS Artifact supports - do not read them as an apiOperation catalogue. Likewise: the single trusted service principal bullet (artifact.amazonaws.com); the role name AWSServiceRoleForArtifact and policy name AWSArtifactServiceRolePolicy; the numbered two-step console procedure for deleting Organization agreements; the Note about deletion failing while the service is using the role; the create/edit/delete section headings and their <a name=...> anchors; the pointer to the IAM 'AWS services that work with IAM' page (its 'Yes' in the 'Service-linked roles' column belongs to that other page, not this one); and the entire 'See also' AI-coding-assistant boilerplate with its aws agent-toolkit search-skills command.
coverageDimensions: REGION: fully given, and it is the only dimension this page measures - 25 named Regions with an explicit Yes/No for service-linked-role support (3 Yes, 22 No). The list is a curated subset of AWS Regions, not all of them: newer Regions (for example ap-east-2, ap-south-2, ap-southeast-4/5/6/7, ca-west-1, eu-central-2, eu-south-2, il-central-1, mx-central-1) and the China Regions are absent, and absence there is silence, not a No. SERVICE: nothing. The page is about one service (AWS Artifact) and names AWS Organizations and IAM only as dependencies; there is no per-service enumeration and any per-service count taken from here is fabricated. RESOURCE TYPE: nothing at all - no resource types are enumerated or scoped anywhere on the page.
trap: The single most likely misparse is treating the four `organizations` API actions (or the trusted principal bullet) as an enumerated coverage list, producing a phantom 4- or 5-value feature - they are policy permissions, not supported/unsupported claims. Runners-up: (1) counting only the Yes rows and reporting 3 supported Regions while dropping the 22 explicitly stated No rows, which loses the page's entire negative signal; (2) counting the header and separator lines and reporting 26 or 27 rows instead of 25; (3) reading the 25-Region list as AWS Artifact's own Region availability, when it is only the Regions where the service-linked role can be used - the lead sentence says the service is available in more Regions than these; (4) treating the missing Regions (China, and the newer Regions) as No, when the page is simply silent about them; (5) harvesting the 'See also' agent-toolkit block or the IAM cross-reference sentence's word 'Yes' as a status value.
